# Ideas 
There are two cases -- the user wants a single variable, and the user wants two variables. I think we should probably just separate these endpoints rather than make some flexible case, because everything -- the way we show the info, etc., will flow downstream from that. 


```{python}
con.execute("DESCRIBE cdc_places").df()
```

```{python}
single_var_sql = """--sql
    SELECT
        p.LocationID,
        p.Measure,
        p.Data_Value_Type,
        p.Data_Value,
        p.bin,
        c.CountyFIPS,
        ST_ASGEOJSON(c.geom) AS geometry
    FROM cdc_places p
    LEFT JOIN vermont_counties c ON p.LocationID = c.CountyFIPS
"""
```


```{python}
where_string = "WHERE p.Measure IN ('Hearing disability among adults', 'Depression among adults') AND p.Data_Value_Type IN ('Crude prevalence')"
res = con.execute(single_var_sql + where_string).df()
res.head()
```

```{python}
measures = res['Measure'].unique()
m1 = res[res.Measure == measures[0]][['LocationID', 'geometry', 'Data_Value', 'bin']]
m2 = res[res.Measure == measures[1]][['LocationID', 'Data_Value', 'bin']]
wide = m1.merge(m2, on='LocationID', suffixes=('_1', '_2'))
wide
wide.columns
```

```{python}

xcmap = plt.cm.viridis_r
ycmap = plt.cm.Blues
n = (3, 3)  # x, y
cmap = xycmap.mean_xycmap(xcmap=xcmap, ycmap=ycmap, n=n)
plt.imshow(cmap, origin='lower')
```

```{python}
def to_rgba(r):
    if pd.isna(r["bin_1"]) or pd.isna(r["bin_2"]):
        return [0, 0, 0, 0]  # transparent for missing
    rgba = cmap[int(r["bin_2"]), int(r["bin_1"])]
    return [round(c * 255) for c in rgba]


wide["color"] = wide.apply(to_rgba, axis=1)
wide.head()
```


Lets take a quick look at how that actually looks...

```{python}
gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(wide, geometry=wide["geometry"].apply(from_geojson))
gdf.plot(color=gdf["color"].apply(lambda c: [v/255 for v in c]))  
```

Not exactly stunning, but this should do okay on the front end. Fine tuning the colormap is something we can do later.

# Clustering Features

```{python}
sme_places = con.execute("""--sql
    SELECT 
        LocationID, 
        Measure, Data_Value, 
        Data_Value_Type
    FROM cdc_places
    WHERE Data_Value_Type IN ('Crude prevalence') 
            AND SME_Highlight = 1
""").df()
# places.head()
pv = sme_places.pivot(columns="Measure", values="Data_Value", index="LocationID")
```

## Cluster Plot and Dendogram

```{python}
sns.clustermap(pv.corr())
```

### Flat Clusters
```{python}
from scipy.cluster.hierarchy import linkage, fcluster
from scipy.spatial.distance import squareform

corr = pv.corr()
dist = 1 - corr.abs()  # co-movement distance, sets diag to zero
Z = linkage(squareform(dist), method="average")

labels = fcluster(Z, t=0.5, criterion="distance")  # k=4 groups
groups = pd.Series(labels, index=corr.index).sort_values()
print(groups)
```

## Parallel Lines Plot
```{python}
pvi = (pv - pv.mean()) / pv.std() # standardize cols
pvi = pvi.reset_index()
```

```{python}
pd.plotting.parallel_coordinates(frame=pvi, class_column="LocationID")
plt.xticks(rotation=90)
plt.show()
```
